source_text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα λέγει πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐ δή που φήσετε περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι μὴ πείσας τοὺς ὧδε ὄντας ἐστέλλετο εἰς ᾅδου πείσων τοὺς ἐκεῖ. κἂν μὴ βούληται οὖν, τοῦτό φαμεν, ὅτι καὶ ἐν σώματι ὢν οὐκ ὀλίγους ἔπεισεν ἀλλὰ τοσούτους. ὡς διὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πειθομένων ἐπιβουλευθῆναι αὐτὸν, καὶ γυμνὴ σώματος γενόμενος ψυχὴ ταῖς γυμναῖς σωμάτων ὡμίλει ψυχαῖς, ἐπιστρέφων κἀκείνων τὰς βουλομένας πρὸς αὐτὸν ἢ ἃς ἑώρα δι᾿ οὓς ᾔδει αὐτὸς λόγους ἐπιτηδειοτέρας.
pass_a_gloss: After these he says to us: surely (οὐ δή που) you will not say concerning him that, not having persuaded (πείθω) those being here, he was dispatched/set out (στέλλομαι) to Hades (ᾅδης) to persuade those there. Even if he does not wish (βούλομαι), we say this: that also being in the body (σῶμα) he persuaded not few but so many, so that through the multitude (πλῆθος) of those persuaded he was plotted against (ἐπιβουλεύω), and having become a soul (ψυχή) naked (γυμνή) of body he conversed (ὁμιλέω) with souls naked of bodies, turning (ἐπιστρέφω) toward himself of those also the willing ones, or those whom he saw, through reasons (λόγοι) which he himself knew, [to be] more suitable (ἐπιτήδειος).
pass_b_english: After this he says to us: “Surely you will not say of him that, having failed to persuade those who were here, he set out for Hades to persuade those who were there.” Whether he likes it or not, we do say this: that while he was in the body he persuaded not a few, but so many that he was plotted against because of the great number of those persuaded; and that when he had become a soul bare of the body, he spoke with souls bare of their bodies, turning to himself those of them also who were willing, or those whom he saw to be better suited, for reasons he himself knew (compare 1 Peter 3:19).

translator_notes: Celsus’s sentence is quoted directly (λέγει πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὅτι ...). ἐστέλλετο may mean “was sent” or “set out”; “set out” is chosen as the middle sense, with “persuade” (πείσων) expressing purpose. Origen does not quote Scripture here, but the preaching of Christ’s soul to the departed is a clear allusion to 1 Peter 3:19 (also 4:6); cited as “compare”. The clause “or those whom he saw ... more suitable” leaves ἐπιτηδειοτέρας without an explicit complement; “better suited” (for conversion) is the plain sense.
